title: HeadCalc convergence-criterion causal isolation at G21I split iterations

boundary_results.interpretation: With compartment balance left at the frozen 1e-12 tolerance, neutralizing head-change, total-balance and ponding criteria individually and jointly does not change the failed physical-solver classification or the 8-attempt backtracking prefix. Therefore compartment balance is necessarily active in the B1 nonconvergence decision among the ordinary non-macropore criteria.
boundary_results.secondary_caution: Relaxing CritDevBalCp changes the backtracking path because the same tolerance participates in Fmax backtracking acceptance. The secondary arms therefore cannot establish compartment balance as the sole original-path blocker.

boundary_results.interpretation: Relaxing only the total-balance criterion switches the B2 status-6 head to physical convergence at the same third Newton iteration with the same three backtracking attempts. HEAD or POND alone do not. This is a clean causal isolation of the total-balance predicate for B2.

bounded_conclusions: The two binary64-adjacent solver bifurcations do not arise from one universal convergence predicate.

At B2, the total-balance convergence check is causally sufficient to explain the split at iteration 3: relaxing TOTAL alone changes the physical solver from nonconverged to converged without changing the three-attempt backtracking trajectory.

At B1, compartment balance is a necessary blocker at iteration 4: every combination of HEAD, TOTAL and POND relaxation leaves the solver nonconverged with exactly the original eight backtracking attempts.

B1 does not support a sole-compartment-blocker claim. Relaxing compartment balance changes backtracking, and compartment-only relaxation still does not converge; relaxing all criteria converges immediately on a different path.

The G21F/G21G islands therefore reflect criterion-sensitive numerical cancellation near the solver acceptance surface, with different adjacent transitions controlled by different aggregate/local balance predicates.
No evidence supports status smoothing, head snapping, tolerance relaxation, retry-depth change or production solver-configuration selection.

The next useful diagnostic is quantitative threshold tomography on the identified predicates: total-balance threshold at B2 can be measured without changing backtracking, while B1 compartment-balance magnitude must be bracketed only over arms that preserve the original eight-attempt path.
next_natural_unit: Open G21K as tolerance-threshold tomography. Quantify the B2 total-balance residual magnitude from a path-preserving total-tolerance bracket/bisection; for B1, scan compartment tolerance but admit only same-backtracking arms, then test whether a path-preserving compartment relaxation exists that reveals any co-blocking HEAD/TOTAL/POND predicate.
